title: JSW Steel Profit Doubles to ₹4,696 Crore in Q1 as Record Sales and Margin Expansion Lift India's Largest Private Steelmaker
excerpt: Higher steel prices, a 46 percent surge in exports and aggressive debt reduction powered a strong quarter for the JSW Group flagship.
body:
• JSW Steel's consolidated net profit more than doubled to ₹4,696 crore in Q1 FY27, up from ₹2,209 crore a year earlier, beating analyst estimates.
  • Total income rose to ₹48,088 crore while EBITDA jumped 32 percent to ₹9,373 crore, driven by higher steel prices and record Q1 sales volumes of 6.25 million tonnes.
  • The company reduced net debt by ₹7,713 crore during the quarter, improving its debt-to-equity ratio to 0.42 from 0.51.
  • JSW Steel commenced construction of a new 2 million tonne steel plant in Andhra Pradesh at an investment of over ₹16,350 crore and approved participation in the JSW One Platforms IPO.

Profit Doubles on Stronger Prices and Record Sales

JSW Steel, India's largest private-sector steelmaker, reported a sharp turnaround in its June quarter results, with consolidated net profit more than doubling to ₹4,696 crore from ₹2,209 crore in the same period last year. Total income climbed to ₹48,088 crore from ₹43,497 crore, while revenue stood at ₹47,364 crore.

The results, announced on Thursday, beat most analyst estimates and sent JSW Steel shares up more than 1 percent on the BSE, where the stock closed at ₹1,238.35.

The improvement was broad-based. EBITDA rose 32 percent year-on-year to ₹9,373 crore, while EBITDA per tonne climbed 27 percent to ₹14,990 — a reflection of firmer domestic steel prices and operational efficiencies. Basic earnings per share more than doubled to ₹19.05 from ₹8.95.

Record Q1 Production and Export Surge

Consolidated crude steel production rose 3.3 percent to 6.59 million tonnes, while saleable steel sales hit a record for any first quarter at 6.25 million tonnes, up 3.6 percent year-on-year. The company focused on flat steel and value-added special products, which typically command higher margins.

Domestic sales accounted for 5.34 million tonnes. Exports surged 46 percent to 0.68 million tonnes, making up 11 percent of sales from Indian operations — a notable jump as the company diversified its revenue base amid improving global demand.

"The investment cycle continues to gain traction, backed by a strong public capex pipeline and sustained activity across commercial real estate, energy, data centres, defence, and maritime sectors."

— JSW Steel, earnings statement

Stronger Balance Sheet, Lower Debt

JSW Steel used the quarter to significantly strengthen its balance sheet. Consolidated net debt declined by ₹7,713 crore from the end of March to ₹46,157 crore as of June 30. The net debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.42 from 0.51, while the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio fell to 1.46 from 1.81.

Finance costs dropped 22.8 percent to ₹1,712 crore, and depreciation expenses declined 15.8 percent to ₹2,137 crore. Total expenses grew at a slower pace than revenue, rising 3.7 percent to ₹41,830 crore, though raw material costs increased 18.4 percent to ₹24,586 crore.

The year-on-year comparison is partly influenced by the deconsolidation of Bhushan Power and Steel Limited, whose steel business left JSW Steel's consolidated accounts on March 27 after JSW Steel and Japan's JFE Steel obtained joint control of the asset. JFE invested a second tranche of ₹7,875 crore by quarter's end.

Expansion and IPO Moves

The company continued its capital expenditure programme at pace. Of the roughly ₹24,000 crore planned for the full fiscal year, ₹4,869 crore was deployed in the first quarter alone. During the quarter, JSW Steel commenced construction of a 2 million tonne per annum steel plant in Andhra Pradesh at an investment exceeding ₹16,350 crore.

At its flagship Vijayanagar plant, the company completed the expansion of blast furnace-3 to 4.5 million tonnes per annum from 3 million tonnes. The furnace was lit in June and has since ramped up to over 80 percent capacity, with incremental volumes expected from the September quarter.

The board also approved JSW Steel's participation in the upcoming initial public offering of JSW One Platforms Limited as a promoter selling shareholder, offering shares worth up to ₹811 crore.

What It Means for Investors

For NRI investors tracking Indian equities, JSW Steel's results reinforce a broader theme: India's infrastructure-led growth cycle is translating into tangible corporate earnings. The steel sector, closely tied to government capital spending on roads, railways, defence and data centres, is emerging as a direct beneficiary. With debt falling and margins expanding, JSW Steel's outlook for the remainder of FY27 depends largely on whether India's public capex momentum holds — and so far, the signals point in that direction.
